narrative:
On September 23, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,650 cases across 49 judges and heard 1,165 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 44.0%. This performance marks a steady efficiency gain compared to recent sessions, outperforming the 42.6% recorded on September 22, 39.5% on September 21, and 42.0% on September 18.

Bench-level output revealed significant variation across courtrooms. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde demonstrated robust progress, hearing 41 of 52 cases (78.8%) in Hall 26, sustaining strong numbers noted earlier in the week. Other high-volume benches with strong disposal included Justice C.M. Poonacha, who heard 78 of 119 matters (65.5%) in Hall 31, and Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum, who concluded 61 of 85 matters (71.8%) in Hall 15. Conversely, several large dockets experienced minimal conversion, including Hall 7 under Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad, where none of the 125 scheduled matters were heard.

Stage-wise analysis shows that early-stage matters drove courtroom activity. Admission was the most frequent listing, converting 369 of 714 scheduled cases (51.7%), an increase from 45.1% recorded on September 22. Orders followed with a 46.9% conversion rate (320 of 682 heard), while Preliminary Hearings achieved 42.9% (173 of 403 heard). Final Hearing matters registered lower conversion at 30.1% (163 of 542 heard), though this improved upon the 24.0% and 27.7% rates recorded on September 22 and September 21, respectively.

In terms of case distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the roster with 1,132 listings, yielding 462 hearings (40.8%), slightly below the previous day's 42.4%. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) reached a 47.7% hearing rate (219 of 459 heard), while Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) closed at 38.9% (111 of 285 heard). Higher clearance efficiency was concentrated in specialized categories, notably Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) at 59.6% (106 of 178 heard) and Civil Revision Petitions (CRP) at 81.2% (13 of 16 heard).
